name: Pike push-up
summary: A push-up with your hips high so you press at an overhead angle. The at-home way to train the shoulder press.
setup: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in and lift your hips until your body makes an upside-down V.
Hands shoulder width or a little wider, fingers spread. Legs as straight as your hamstrings allow; bend the knees if you need to.
Shift your weight forward so your shoulders sit over or slightly in front of your hands.

steps.text: Push the floor away and reach your shoulders up toward your ears, as you would at the top of an overhead press.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward a spot on the floor about a hand length in front of your fingers. Head and hands form a triangle.
Stop just before your head touches. Hips stay high over your shoulders.
Press back up along the same line until your arms are straight.

jointCues.cue: Bend back toward your knees at about 45 degrees, not straight out to the sides.
jointCues.why: Same reason as the overhead press: elbows slightly forward keep the shoulder in its strongest, roomiest path.

jointCues.cue: At the top, push tall and let them rotate up toward your ears.
jointCues.why: Overhead pressing needs the shoulder blade to rotate upward. Pinning them down blocks it.

jointCues.cue: Moves forward of your hands, not straight down between them.
jointCues.why: Lowering between the hands turns it into a short, wrist-heavy push-up.

jointCues.cue: Stay high and stacked over the shoulders.
jointCues.why: Dropping the hips makes it a regular push-up and takes the load off the shoulders.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press up.

mistakes.fix: Walk your feet closer to your hands.
Turn the elbow creases forward and aim the elbows at your knees.
Lower to a spot in front of your fingertips.

safety: Use a folded towel under your head the first few sessions. Stop if you feel neck pain.

cues.text: Hips high, stacked over the shoulders
Top: push tall, shoulder blades rotate up toward the ears
Head travels forward of your hands: a triangle
Elbows point back toward your knees
